newsitem.title: INDIA: India HFCL has turnkey orders of $70 mln.
newsitem.headline: India HFCL has turnkey orders of $70 mln.

text.p: India's telecommunications firm Himachal Futuristic Communication Ltd (HFCL) said on Thursday its turnkey division had bagged orders worth 2.5 billion rupees ($70 million) in 1996/97 (April-March).
"We expect 3.0-4.0 billion rupees of orders during the next financial year," Y.L. Agarwal, executive director of HFCL, told a news conference.
The turnkey division was set up in early 1995 to grab a slice of the growing telecommunications services and equipment market, Agarwal told Reuters after the news conference.
Agrawal said the turnkey division offered a complete solution to clients from "concept to execution of projects".
"Most of these orders have come from private sector operators for basic and cellular services," a company statement said.
In the next financial year beginning April 1, HFCL's turnkey division expects export orders worth 500 million rupees ($14 million) from South Asian, African and West Asian countries, Agarwal said.
The company has received orders for radio pagers from South Korea, Belgium and Germany, he added.

The little known company from the northern state of Himachal Pradesh captured public attention in 1995 when it offered a staggering $27 billion for licences to set up basic telephone services in nine of India's 21 telephone zones.

But HFCL ran into a legal dispute with the Indian government over financial modalities when it was expected to obtain licences to set up telephone services in four of the zones for which it was entitled to receive licences.
India had put a ceiling on the number of licences a company can operate.
The legal dispute is being heard in Indian courts.
India allowed private firms to set up telephone services under its economic liberalisation programme launched in 1991. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
